messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a small spike of 502/503s from the inference edge in eu-west-1 around the GPU downscale window. Symptoms look like headless services temporarily returning no endpoints. :thinking:

jon: repro? any pods terminating at the same time as the scale event?

maria: yeah the GPU node drain started ~1769998820, we drain 4 spot nodes. App pods are terminating, and for ~30s the headless svc for `inference-backend` had zero endpoints from the consumer side. k8s API still showed endpointslices present but kube-proxy on some nodes didn't have rules.

sam: can you paste `kubectl get endpointslice -n inference -o wide` around that time? suspect slice label mismatch or controller lag.

maria: pasted from node where client failed:
```
NAME                                  ADDRESS-TYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS
inference-xxxx-abc-0001               IPv4           8080    pod-a1
inference-xxxx-abc-0002               IPv4           8080    pod-a2
```
But on the nodes with failures `ipvsadm -L -n` showed no backends for the headless service IP.

lia: interesting — endpointSlice exists but kube-proxy hasn't programmed ephemeral rules. Did kube-proxy log `Failed to sync endpoints`?

maria: yes saw repeated `E0504 12:14:42 node.go:xxx] Failed to sync endpoints for...` in kube-proxy on two nodes.

infra-bot: alert: node/eu-west-spot-42 drained (preemptible) — 4 pods evicted.

jon: possible race: endpointSlice controller and kube-proxy updates crossing with node drain causing kube-proxy to temporarily remove rules. Also we recently enabled topology aware routing & endpointSlice hints for headless svcs — could be the hint controller removing endpoints from some nodes until cache warms.

sam: also check CoreDNS: if the DNS SRV/ A results switch to none, clients will consider the service unreachable. Run `dig +short @10.96.0.10 inference-backend.default.svc.cluster.local` from a failing node.

maria: did that — dig returned A records in API time but resolution locally failed during window. CoreDNS logs had spikes of `no such endpoint` lookups.

lia: what's the mitigation? we can't stop spot drains.

jon: short term: add a small deprovisioning drain delay on GPU pool (eg 40s) so kube-proxy & endpointSlice propagate. Also consider setting kube-proxy mode to `ipvs` on critical edge nodes (less churn) and bump endpointSlice sync period.

sam: another mitigation — for headless services that back L7 frontends, consider enabling `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` on the fronting Service (if applicable) or add a tiny readiness probe delay so pods don't become non-ready until kube-proxy programs rules.

maria: created the follow-up ticket: https://redwood.example.com/infra/ops/tickets/INF-3251 — summary: "race during spot drain leads to temporary headless svc no-endpoints on kube-proxy". Action items: 1) add 40s drain delay (maria) 2) experiment with kube-proxy ipvs on a canary (jon) 3) increase endpointslice controller resync (sam).

deploy-bot: rollout started: kube-proxy-canary -> eu-west-1 nodes (3 nodes) :rocket:

lia: :thumbsup: will watch logs and set an alert for `headless svc zero backends` metric.

maria: thanks — will post follow-up after canary. :eyes:
